summary: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry table gives ordinary passport holders of, for example, Germany, France, the United States, the United Kingdom and China visa-free stays of up to 30 days, and citizens of Russia, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan up to 90 days. overstay.text: Under the Code of Administrative Offences, a foreigner who does not leave Kazakhstan after the legal period expires receives a warning if within three days, a fine of ten monthly calculation indices for more than three and up to five days, and fifteen for more than five and up to ten days. Evading departure for more than ten days is punished by a fine of twenty-five monthly calculation indices or administrative expulsion. Under the Law on Migration, immigrants previously expelled from Kazakhstan are barred from entry for five years from the expulsion.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Kazakhstan?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry table gives ordinary passport holders of, for example, Germany, the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Japan and China visa-free stays of up to 30 days, and citizens of Russia, Belarus, Ukraine, Moldova, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Mongolia and Turkey, among others, up to 90 days. Tourist electronic visas are issued to citizens of the states on the Ministry's list through the Visa and Migration Portal, in accordance with a valid invitation from the Kazakh side.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Kazakhstan visa-free?
faq.answer: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry table gives ordinary passport holders of, for example, Germany, the United States, the United Kingdom and China up to 30 days. Other allowances differ: up to 90 days for citizens of Russia, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan and of Albania, Andorra, Saint Kitts and Nevis, San Marino and Turkey; up to 60 days for the Dominican Republic; up to 28 days for Barbados; and up to 14 days for India, Iran, Hong Kong and Macao. The UK government tells British nationals they can visit without a visa for up to 30 days, but must not stay more than 90 days without a visa in any 180-day period.

faq.question: Do I need to register after arriving in Kazakhstan?
faq.answer: The UK government says your hotel or the person hosting you must register your arrival with the Kazakh authorities within 3 working days of your arrival. Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry says foreign citizens who have valid electronic visas are exempted from registration in migration authorities.

faq.question: How does the Kazakhstan eVisa work?
faq.answer: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry says the electronic visa is issued through the Visa and Migration Portal (vmp.gov.kz) in accordance with a valid invitation from the Kazakh side: you register on the portal, enter the invitation number sent by the inviting side, pay the consular fee online and print the visa. The consular fee for a single tourist visa is 60 US dollars. A tourist eVisa is issued with a single entry for up to 90 days and the right to stay no more than 30 days, and the Ministry's page says eVisa holders can enter and exit only through the checkpoints of the international airports of Nur-Sultan and Almaty; the Embassy in Washington's January 2026 notice says only through border crossing points of the international airports of Kazakhstan.

faq.question: Can Russian and other CIS citizens enter Kazakhstan without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry table lists visa-free stays of up to 90 days for ordinary passport holders of Russia, Belarus, Ukraine, Moldova, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan; for Armenia and Azerbaijan it gives up to 90 days within 180 days.
